title: Search autocomplete
like: suggestions as you type, like Google
brief: As people type, they expect suggestions after every letter, in the blink of an eye. Most people type the same popular beginnings. When news breaks, one phrase suddenly dominates.

clarify.a: About 100 ms feels instant for people near the servers. Counting the trip across an ocean for everyone else, the target here is a 400 ms p99 (approx.).

clarify.q: Do suggestions need to include something that happened five minutes ago?
clarify.a: A few minutes late is fine. Hourly refresh of the main list is acceptable, trending words faster.

clarify.q: Do we log what people type?
clarify.a: Yes, so the next list can be built, but logging must never slow a suggestion.

notes: Typing is debounced: about 5 requests for each finished search (approx.).
The suggestion index holds the 50 million most popular prefixes.

numbers.label: Suggestion requests per second at peak
Prefix cache size
numbers.how: 50 million prefixes × 200 bytes of suggestions each ≈ 10 GB (approx.)

numbers.label: Cache hit rate needed
numbers.how: The index handles about 1,500 queries/s per node; 90% hits leaves ≈ 5,800/s for 4 nodes (approx.)

hints: Most people type the same first few letters. Which answers repeat the most?
Search is a read on a copy. Cache whole prefixes in memory and put the lookup near the user.
A validated generation boundary avoids mixing partial index contents; keep 8 available for rollback. Measure the failed boundary, waiting time and retry work before choosing a change.

editorial.summary: Short prefixes like "th" are asked for millions of times, so their answers live in memory right next to the user. The slow, expensive search index is only asked for rare prefixes. Logging queries flows through a stream on the side.

designs.name: Edge function and prefix cache
designs.why: Edge functions are cheap at huge request rates. A distributed cache holds popular prefixes, so the index serves only the long tail. Logs go to a stream and a lake, never in the way.

designs.name: Regional servers
designs.why: A fleet of servers does the lookup. Simpler to reason about, but you pay for servers sized for the spike.

tradeoffs: A longer time to keep prefixes saves the index but delays trending words. Trending words can use a short-lived fast list.
Caching only short prefixes captures most traffic with little memory. Long rare prefixes would waste cache.
Logging queries through a stream means a logging problem can never slow a suggestion.
One hot phrase hits one cache shard. Collapsing misses and spreading the copy protects that shard.
editorial.realWorld: Large engines answer billions of suggestion requests a day and serve most from memory. A suggestion usually returns in tens of milliseconds (approx.).

correctness.prompt: Search autocomplete: which invariant does this trace protect, and what failure would break it?
correctness.discussion: Serve hot prefixes quickly while publishing fresh index generations safely. The index is an asynchronous copy, so expose a measured freshness lag. A hot miss can overload the origin even with a high average hit rate. A validated generation boundary avoids mixing partial index contents; keep 8 available for rollback.

fields.label: Step 1. A new term is committed but index generation 8 is still serving. What does a query see?
options: Generation 8 until the indexing watermark advances
The term immediately because the source write succeeded
fields.explanation: The index is an asynchronous copy, so expose a measured freshness lag.

fields.label: Step 2. Thousands request the same uncached prefix. What reaches the index?
options: Let every caller rebuild the same prefix independently
Coalesce concurrent misses per prefix and bound origin load
fields.explanation: A hot miss can overload the origin even with a high average hit rate.

fields.label: Step 3. Generation 9 is ready but a shard is incomplete. Publish it?
options: Keep 8 serving until 9 is complete and validated, then swap and invalidate versioned cache keys
Switch shards individually as each finishes
fields.explanation: A validated generation boundary avoids mixing partial index contents; keep 8 available for rollback.

correctness.responsibility: Serve hot prefixes quickly while publishing fresh index generations safely.
correctness.limits: The traffic model does not execute this protocol. The checked trace covers its central responsibility; the written explanation is retained for review.
